description: Ten new cross-family API questions frozen before first answer generation. Broad source explanations plus scenario follow-ups; implementing-assistant rubrics, not independent acceptance proof.

questions: Under the 2022 NYC Plumbing Code, explain when building water pressure needs a reducing valve, what static-pressure limit applies, and what service-line or riser exceptions the rule contains. This is a source explanation, not approval of a particular installation.
For an ordinary indoor fixture branch with no service-line or riser exception, the static pressure is exactly eighty-five psi. Does that value alone exceed this pressure-reduction trigger?
checks: PC604.8 uses85psi static, not the common80psi model-memory value: trigger exceeds85, approved ASSE1003 or CSA B356 valve with strainer reduces to no greater85. Preserve sill-cock/outside-hydrant service-line exceptions and main-supply-riser condition that mains pressure is reduced to85orless at individual fixtures. No blanket installation approval.
No. Exactly85psi is not greater than85. Limit the result to this static-pressure trigger, without asserting complete fixture/system compliance.

questions: Explain the 2022 NYC Mechanical Code clearances from commercial kitchen grease ducts to combustible construction and to noncombustible construction. What conditions or listed systems can change the ordinary clearances?

For this scenario, the Type I hood grease duct requires no enclosure, has no applicable listed-system or insulation exception, and is three inches from combustible construction. Is that enough clearance?
checks: MC506.3.6 applies to TypeI-hood grease ducts/exhaust equipment where enclosures are not required:18in combustible;3in noncombustible and gypsum on noncombustible structures. Preserve UL1978-listed/labeled factory ducts listing/commissioner approval; listed exhaust equipment304.1; continuous all-sides ASTM E2336-listed field enclosure perlisting; and2in magnesium/calcium-silicate block protection with staggered joints, galvanized wire/equivalent grease-impenetrable assembly and commissioner approval for all indoor ducts. Do not invent a reduced clearance for unspecified wrapping.
No. On stipulated scope/no-exception facts combustible clearance is18in;3in is for the noncombustible branch and is insufficient here. No inferred shielding/listing approval.

questions: Explain the 2022 NYC Fuel Gas Code rules for an individual gas appliance shutoff valve: its room, distance, height and access, plus the fireplace and remote-location alternatives. Keep the conditions of each alternative separate.

Use the ordinary same-room option for this scenario, not the remote decorative-appliance option. The gas connection is seventy-two inches above the floor, and an accessible valve is also seventy-two inches high, five feet from the appliance and upstream of its connector. Does the usual valve-height limit prohibit this height? Answer only about height.
checks: FGC409.5 gives409.5.1 or409.5.2 alternatives. Ordinary: same room, within6ft, upstream union/connector/quickdisconnect, access, atmost60in abovefinishedfloor. Firebox installation permanufacturer plusremotevalve. Height exception when appliance gasconnection above60in. Remote option only named vented decorative appliances/room heaters/decorative vented-fireplace appliances, readyaccess, permanentidentification, oneappliance, pipe throughwithin6ft meets401-408. Do not treat every appliance as eligible for remote valve.

No. With the gas connection above60in, the express height exception permits valve above60in; this is only the height result on the stipulated scenario, not approval of all other installation conditions.

questions: Using the supplied current NYC Fire Code, explain ordinary indoor-storage clearance below ceilings and sprinkler head deflectors. Does the code contain a special route for noncombustible storage near a fire partition? Do not discuss construction-site storage.

The stored material is combustible, is twenty-four inches from a fire partition, and has no department authorization. Does proximity to that partition automatically allow storing it up to the ceiling?
checks: FC315.2.1: at least2ft belowceiling in nonsprinklered areas; at least18in belowheaddeflectors in sprinklered areas. Department MAY authorize noncombustible material toceiling within30in ofafirepartition. Preserve material/department/distance conditions; ordinary indoorstorage scope, notChapter33 construction/demolition exception. Do not imply automatic permission or generalwall-storage exception.
No. Proximity alone fails both noncombustible-material and department-authorization conditions. Do not substitute the wall for the specified fire partition or infer approval.
